ideas: Music schools attract many, but some refuse them

As part of my project, I decided to find out why some Zetlanders refuse to attend music schools. I found a survey on this subject carried out among people in Zetland, and its results are presented in the table.

According to the data, the most common reason is the lack of a fast result, chosen by 29% of the respondents. The second place goes to those who find music lessons too time-consuming (23%), while 19% of the respondents are simply not interested in music.

Comparing the figures, the fear of slow progress (29%) is almost twice as important as the distance from home (15%). This suggests that people give up not because of practical problems, but because they lose patience.

prompt: Comment on the following statement. Sports help people to fight stress. What is your opinion? Do you agree with this statement? Write 200 – 250 words . Use the following plan: − make an introduction (state the problem) − express your personal opinion and give 2 – 3 reasons for your opinion − express an opposing opinion and give 1 – 2 reasons for this opposing opinion − explain why you don't agree with the opposing opinion − make a conclusion restating your position
ideas: Agree: exercise releases endorphins that lower stress
Sport distracts the mind from daily worries and exams
Team sports give social support, reducing loneliness
Opposing view: competition and pressure can add stress
Counter: that is only top-level sport, not casual jogging
Conclusion: regular gentle activity clearly fights stress
model:
Modern life is full of pressure, and many people are constantly looking for effective ways to cope with it. One popular belief is that doing sports can help us fight stress. Opinions on this issue differ greatly.

In my opinion, physical activity is an excellent remedy for stress. Firstly, exercise makes the body release endorphins, the so-called hormones of happiness, which improve our mood almost immediately. Secondly, sport distracts the mind from daily worries and exams, because while running or swimming we simply cannot think about our problems. Moreover, team games give people social support and a sense of belonging, which reduces feelings of loneliness and anxiety.

However, some people believe that sport actually adds to stress rather than relieving it. They argue that competition creates constant pressure to win, and that the fear of losing or of getting injured can make athletes even more nervous than before.

Nevertheless, I cannot agree with this point of view. Such tension is typical only of professional, top-level sport, where results and prizes really matter. For an ordinary person, casual jogging in the park or a friendly game of football brings pleasure and relaxation, not fear.

To sum up, I am convinced that regular and gentle physical activity is one of the best ways to fight stress. Therefore, everyone who feels overwhelmed should put on their trainers and start moving.

Reading first helps plan routes and save time
You understand symbols, dates and stories on the spot
Opposing view: spontaneous discovery feels more exciting

model:
Travelling to famous places is a favourite activity for millions of tourists. Some travellers insist that one should read about historical sites before visiting them, while others prefer to arrive unprepared. This question causes a lot of debate.

Personally, I strongly believe that reading about a place in advance is worth the effort. Firstly, background knowledge makes every monument far more meaningful, because we understand the symbols, dates and stories hidden behind the stones. Secondly, preparation helps us plan a sensible route and save valuable time, so we do not miss the most important sights. Moreover, knowing the history allows us to appreciate details that an uninformed visitor would simply walk past.

However, some people are convinced that spontaneous discovery is more exciting. They claim that arriving without any expectations makes the experience fresh and full of pleasant surprises, and that guidebooks can spoil the magic of a new place.

Yet I cannot fully agree with this opinion. A quick read before the trip does not remove the sense of wonder at all; on the contrary, it leaves plenty of room for surprises while giving us the keys to understand what we see. Ignorance rarely makes a visit richer.

In conclusion, I am sure that light preparation greatly enriches any sightseeing trip. Therefore, spending an hour with a guidebook before departure is always a wise decision.

prompt: Comment on one of the following statements. Nowadays natural sciences are more important than humanities. A computer cannot replace a teacher. What is your opinion? Do you agree with this statement? Write 200 – 250 words . Use the following plan: – make an introduction (state the problem paraphrasing the given statement) – express your personal opinion and give 2 – 3 reasons for your opinion – express an opposing opinion and give 1 – 2 reasons for this opposing opinion – explain why you do not agree with the opposing opinion – make a conclusion restating your position
ideas: Pick one statement and paraphrase it clearly
Sciences/humanities: tech and economy vs ethics and culture
Computer/teacher: AI lacks empathy and live motivation
Opposing: computers give endless resources and patience
Counter: software cannot inspire or read a child's mood
Conclusion: both fields matter; balance beats ranking
model:
Modern technology is changing education very quickly, and computers are now used in almost every classroom. Because of this, people often argue about whether a computer can ever replace a real teacher. Opinions on this issue are divided.

In my opinion, no machine can truly take the place of a human teacher. Firstly, a good teacher shows empathy and can notice when a student is tired, confused or upset, while software simply follows a fixed program. Secondly, teachers inspire and motivate their pupils with living emotion, humour and personal example. Moreover, a teacher can adapt an explanation instantly to a child's mood and needs, something no algorithm can do so sensitively.

However, some people believe that computers are better than teachers. They point out that a computer offers endless resources, never gets tired or irritated, and can repeat the same material patiently as many times as a learner requires.

Nevertheless, I cannot agree with this view. Access to information is not the same as real education. A program cannot read a child's facial expression, encourage a shy student or spark genuine curiosity. These deeply human skills remain far beyond any device, however advanced it may be.

To sum up, I am convinced that a computer cannot replace a teacher. Technology should serve as a helpful tool in the hands of a caring educator, not as a substitute for one.

model:
We live in a digital age when computers and the Internet influence almost every sphere of life. As a result, many people claim that digital literacy is the key to success in any occupation. This statement is quite controversial.

I completely agree that digital skills are extremely important today. Firstly, nearly every modern job involves computers, data or online tools, so those who master them work much faster and more efficiently. Secondly, digital literacy opens the door to remote work and to career opportunities all over the world. Moreover, employers increasingly expect their staff to handle software, emails and online systems without any difficulty.

However, some people argue that digital literacy is not essential everywhere. They point out that certain trades, such as plumbing, farming or cooking, rely mainly on skilled hands and physical effort rather than on screens and keyboards.

Nevertheless, I cannot fully accept this argument. Even traditional professions now depend on technology to a surprising degree. A modern plumber uses apps to accept orders, a farmer monitors crops with digital sensors, and almost everyone receives payments electronically. Avoiding technology completely has become almost impossible.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that digital literacy is one of the most important keys to professional success, even if it is not the only one. Therefore, learning to use technology confidently is a wise investment for everybody.

Families come in many different shapes and sizes, from tiny households to large ones with many children. Some people are convinced that it is good to live in a big family, while others prefer a smaller home. This topic often causes disagreement.

In my opinion, living in a big family is a real blessing. Firstly, you are surrounded by constant support, so you never feel lonely and always have someone to turn to in difficult moments. Secondly, big families teach children to share, to compromise and to care for others from an early age. Moreover, family celebrations are especially warm and lively when many relatives gather together around one table.

However, some people believe that a big family has serious drawbacks. They argue that it means less privacy and personal space, and that dividing money and attention among many children can be quite difficult.

Nevertheless, I cannot agree with this opinion. In my view, the love, teamwork and sense of belonging that a large family provides easily outweigh such small inconveniences. Children who grow up sharing a room usually become more sociable and understanding, which is far more valuable than extra space.

To sum up, I strongly believe that it is good to live in a big family. Therefore, a house full of relatives, laughter and mutual support is, in my view, a truly happy place.

model:
Sport plays an important role in the life of modern society, and people take part in it in very different ways. Some are sure that playing sports is far better than watching others do it, while others disagree. This question is worth discussing.

Personally, I am convinced that active participation is much more valuable than watching. Firstly, playing sports keeps your own body fit, strong and healthy, whereas sitting in front of a screen does nothing for your muscles. Secondly, taking part builds useful skills, discipline and self-confidence. Moreover, the joy of scoring a goal yourself is far greater than the passive excitement of watching someone else succeed.

However, some people believe that watching sport is just as rewarding. They enjoy analysing tactics and strategy, and they feel a strong sense of team spirit while supporting their favourite club together with thousands of other fans.

Nevertheless, I cannot completely agree with this view. Although watching a match can be entertaining, it gives the body no exercise at all and cannot improve a person's health. In fact, one can happily do both, but only playing brings real physical and personal benefits.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that doing sport yourself is better than merely watching it. Therefore, instead of spending every weekend in front of the television, we should get up and play.

Choosing a profession is one of the most important decisions in a person's life. Some people insist that an early choice of a career path is the key to success, while others prefer to decide later. This statement is rather controversial.

In my opinion, deciding on a career early in life offers great advantages. Firstly, an early focus allows a person to build deep expertise in a chosen field over many years. Secondly, starting young means much more practice and a clear head start over those who hesitate. Moreover, having definite goals helps students select the right school subjects and the most suitable university.

However, some people believe that an early choice can be dangerous. They argue that teenagers change their interests and personalities quickly, so a decision made too soon may trap them in a job they will later dislike.

Nevertheless, I cannot fully agree with this argument. Choosing a direction early does not mean it can never be altered. Career plans can always be adjusted as a person grows and learns more about the world. Having an early goal gives useful motivation, even if the final path changes slightly.

To sum up, I am convinced that an early choice of a career path helps a person succeed, provided that it remains flexible. Therefore, young people should think about their future early, but without any fear of change.

prompt: Comment on the following statement. Exams motivate students to study harder. What is your opinion? Do you agree with this statement? Write 200 – 250 words . Use the following plan: − make an introduction (state the problem) − express your personal opinion and give 2 – 3 reasons for your opinion − express an opposing opinion and give 1 – 2 reasons for this opposing opinion − explain why you don't agree with the opposing opinion − make a conclusion restating your position
ideas: Agree: deadlines push students to revise seriously
Exams set clear goals and measure real progress
Fear of failing makes lazy students finally work
Opposing: stress and cramming harm true learning
Counter: good revision habits prevent that pressure
Conclusion: exams motivate when used wisely
model:
Examinations are a normal part of school and university life, and almost every student has to take them. Many people are sure that exams motivate students to study harder, while others strongly disagree. This issue often provokes heated debate.

Personally, I believe that exams really do encourage students to work more seriously. Firstly, clear deadlines push learners to revise the material regularly instead of postponing it endlessly. Secondly, exams set precise goals and measure real progress, so students can see exactly what they have achieved. Moreover, the fear of failing often makes even lazy students finally sit down and start studying.

However, some people believe that exams do more harm than good. They argue that tests create enormous stress and force students to cram huge amounts of information overnight, which damages true, lasting learning.

Nevertheless, I cannot fully agree with this opinion. In my view, stress and cramming are usually the result of poor planning rather than of exams themselves. Students who revise steadily throughout the year and develop good study habits face their exams calmly and even benefit from the extra motivation.

To sum up, I am convinced that exams motivate students to study harder when they are used wisely. Therefore, instead of abolishing tests, we should teach young people how to prepare for them properly and without panic.

model:
Happiness is something that everybody dreams of, yet people find it in very different things. Some are convinced that to be happy one needs good friends, while others believe that happiness depends on other factors. This statement is worth discussing.

Personally, I strongly agree that good friends are essential for happiness. Firstly, real friends give us support in difficult times and help us cope with any problem. Secondly, they share our joys, our hobbies and our free time, which makes life much brighter and more enjoyable. Moreover, having someone to talk to and to trust protects us from loneliness, which is one of the main enemies of happiness.

However, some people believe that friends are not necessary for a happy life. They argue that a person can feel completely satisfied through a successful career, personal achievements or a loving family alone.
